shortDescription: The US owner of Poundland is trying to find a solution for the troubled British discount retailer that preserves as many jobs as possible, it said on Thursday.

children: The US owner of Poundland is trying to find a solution for the troubled British discount retailer that preserves as many jobs as possible, it said on Thursday.

“We are pursuing all avenues through the sale process to find a solution which protects as many jobs as possible and preserves value," a spokesperson at Gordon Brothers on the Poundland sale process said
They said work was continuing at pace with "active discussions on offers with interested parties"

Last Thursday, Poundland, which trades from more than 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, employing about 12,000, filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, giving the business 10 working days to find a rescue deal
Gordon Brothers' stewardship of Poundland, which it purchased last year for a nominal £1 from Warsaw-listed Pepco Group

The spokesperson defended its ownership, saying when Gordon Brothers acquired the business, it was in distress, required a radical restructure, urgent operational change and significant funding, which it provided
The UK government has said it wants to see an outcome that protects as many jobs as possible and keeps as much of the business trading as possible
Poundland operates a distribution centre in Prime Minister Andy Burnham's Makerfield constituency in northwest England
